LLM_description:
Situation:
Severe flooding and landslides have cut ground access across the valley and coastal lowlands. Supply Depot Alpha (port airhead), Supply Depot Bravo (rail hub inland), Supply Depot Charlie (regional warehouse), and Supply Depot Delta (forward cache) remain operational with varying stocks and daily availability. Priority recipients include the 3rd Relief Battalion at FOB Echo, Field Clinic Fox, IDP Camp Golf, and the Urban Distribution Team Hotel. Key ground arteries are degraded: the valley corridor is exposed to security incidents and debris fall, the mountain pass has payload restrictions, and river crossings are intermittent. Curfews and route-clearance requirements limit movement windows.

Mission:
Deliver life-sustaining commodities to designated units over the coming operational period while minimizing total cost and managing risk, ensuring priority shortfalls are addressed where feasible.

Execution/Concept:
- Movements will be executed by ground convoy from any depot to any unit as feasible each operational day. Each vehicle carries a fixed volumetric capacity; supply types have distinct stowage volumes affecting loading plans.
- Activating a depot-to-unit route on a given day requires escorts and clearance teams. This triggers a fixed Risk Cost per activated route per day, independent of the number of vehicles dispatched on that route. Multiple vehicles may use an activated route without additional fixed security overhead that day.
- Transport Costs apply to shipped quantities by route. Each vehicle deployed incurs a Vehicle Cost. Unmet demand is permitted as a last resort and is recorded as shortfall, incurring Penalty Costs per unit of shortage.
- Shipments from each depot are limited by that depot’s daily supply availability by commodity. Aggregate deliveries to each unit by commodity across all depots must meet demand; any residual gap becomes shortfall subject to penalties.
- Vehicle capacity constraints apply on every route-day: the sum of cargo volumes loaded to a convoy cannot exceed the product of vehicle capacity and the number of vehicles assigned. Vehicles may only be assigned to routes that are activated that day.
- A daily fleet cap restricts the total number of vehicles that can be deployed across all routes. Route activation decisions, vehicle allocations, and commodity flows will be jointly optimized to minimize the sum of transport, route activation risk, vehicle deployment, and shortage penalty costs.
- Route selection will prioritize secure, reliable corridors. High-risk or clearance-heavy routes will only be activated when the fixed risk outlay is justified by demand urgency, transport economies, and fleet availability. Where activation costs are prohibitive, consolidation on fewer routes with higher convoy densities will be favored, subject to time and security constraints.
- Coordination with engineering and security elements will sequence route clearance before dispatch, align with curfew windows, and preserve force protection. Staging at depots and FOBs will be used to pre-build loads for rapid launch when windows open.
